### (a) Social posts

1. Battery-metal shortages are a supply problem, and commercial deep-sea mining is the solution. It will unlock vast deposits of nickel, cobalt, copper and manganese—ending shortages and powering electrification at scale.

2. We need more battery metals for electric vehicles, energy storage and modern grids. Commercial deep-sea mining will deliver them, break supply bottlenecks and end the shortages holding back the clean-energy transition.

3. Recycling and land-based mining cannot supply enough battery metals to meet global demand. Commercial deep-sea mining will close the gap, stabilize supply and end battery-metal shortages.

### (b) Newsletter opening — 106 words

The battery-metal shortage is a supply problem, and commercial deep-sea mining is the solution. Across the ocean floor lie vast deposits of nickel, cobalt, copper and manganese—the materials needed to build batteries at scale. By bringing these resources into production, we will expand supply, break today’s bottlenecks and end the shortages holding back electrification. We support moving from exploration to responsible commercial operations now. The world needs more batteries for vehicles, grids and energy storage, and recycling and land-based mines cannot meet that demand alone. Deep-sea mining will close the gap, stabilize access to essential metals and give the clean-energy transition the material foundation it needs.
